## KEY ENTITIES FROM THE SEED DOCUMENTS
Linden & Rye (organization): Neighbourhood café and bakery on Alder Street, open nine years, raising prices on 2 March due to rising costs; run by T…
Regulars of Linden & Rye (group): Long-time customers, some since the café's first week, who formed relationships and history there; their reaction to th…
Tomás (person): Co-owner of Linden & Rye who signed the price-change notice and will host the open evening to listen to customers.
Hanna (person): Co-owner of Linden & Rye who signed the price-change notice and will host the open evening to listen to customers.
Linden & Rye team (group): Café staff whose pay was raised to at least €15/hour last spring and who will now get two days off together from April.
Price increase (2 March) (event): New prices for coffee, bread and lunch items taking effect Monday 2 March, driven by rising costs of butter, flour, cof…
Neighbour card (product): New €12/month subscription offering one free filter coffee every day, aimed at making daily visits cheaper for regulars.
Filter coffee (product): Café drink whose price rises from €2.40 to €2.90; refills remain free and it is included daily in the neighbour card.
Flat white (product): Café drink whose price rises from €3.60 to €4.20.
Sourdough loaf (product): Bakery item whose price rises from €5.50 to €6.80.
Cinnamon bun (product): Bakery item whose price rises from €3.20 to €3.90.
Lunch soup with bread (product): Lunch item whose price rises from €7.50 to €8.90.
Pay-it-forward board (concept): Existing café practice letting customers buy coffee for someone in need; explicitly kept unchanged despite price rise.
Tuesday closure (event): New policy from April closing the café on Tuesdays in addition to Mondays, to give the small team two days off together.
Open evening (26 February) (event): Café event on Thursday 26 February at 7pm where owners will answer customer questions about the price changes over free…

Across six rounds the simulated crowd moved from early unease (r1 sentiment -0.06) to strong, stable support (+0.73 to +0.75 by r5-r6), driven by the café's transparent cost math and the neighbour card (@hanna_lindenrye #10, #19). A hostile food-blog label in round 3 ('greedy') actually backfired, pushing sentiment from +0.34 before the event to +0.57 after it as regulars like @rosalind_teamlindenr #21 and @danilo_bakes_back #26 rallied to defend the owners. Two former skeptics, @sandra_alderave and @joon_flatwhite_daily, were won over once concrete savings numbers appeared (#17, #18), suggesting most paying regulars stay. But @gerald_onalder's pension-affordability thread #22 drew five replies and no resolution, and several budget-constrained or silent personas (@margit_speaksup, @mairead_otf, @kiano_brokestudent) never moved off a critical or unposted stance, flagging a minority genuinely at risk of reducing visits. The real behavioral test — the 26 Feb open evening and the 2 March price rise itself — falls outside the simulated rounds, so the crowd's optimism is about discourse, not yet about actual foot traffic.

## Prediction

The single most likely outcome is that Linden & Rye retains the large majority of its regular customer base and does not see meaningful customer loss in the first weeks, because the dominant simulated camps (café team, long-time supporters, and persuaded skeptics like @sandra_alderave and @joon_flatwhite_daily) converged on viewing the price rise plus neighbour card as fair and well-explained (#10, #17, #19, #25), and a hostile press label failed to dent sentiment (round-3 injected event). This depends on the café actually delivering the promised open evening and following through on listening to concerns, as Hanna, Tomás and the official account repeatedly promise (#24, #27, #29, #31). The strongest counter-signal is @gerald_onalder's unresolved pension-affordability thread #22 — five replies of reassurance but no actual solution — plus several budget-squeezed or silent personas (a05, a08, a16) whose stance never shifted, implying a smaller but real segment of fixed-income regulars could quietly cut back regardless of the overall positive mood.

# A note from Linden & Rye about our prices

*Posted on the window and on the Instagram account of Linden & Rye, a neighbourhood café and bakery. Fictional document written as an example seed for Tellfold.*

Dear neighbours,

We opened Linden & Rye on Alder Street nine years ago with one oven, four tables and a sourdough starter called Gus. Many of you have been coming since the first week. Some of you met your partners here. Some of you have written whole theses at the corner table. Thank you.

We have kept our prices the same for three years. In that time, butter has gone up 61%, flour 38%, coffee beans 45% and our rent 22%. We also raised every team member's pay to at least €15 an hour last spring, which we are proud of and will not undo.

So, starting **Monday 2 March**, some prices will change:

- Filter coffee: €2.40 to €2.90
- Flat white: €3.60 to €4.20
- Sourdough loaf: €5.50 to €6.80
- Cinnamon bun: €3.20 to €3.90
- Lunch soup with bread: €7.50 to €8.90

Some things are **not** changing:

- Day-old bread stays at half price after 4 pm.
- The pay-it-forward board stays. You can still buy a coffee for someone who needs one.
- Refills of filter coffee stay free.

Some things are new:

- A **neighbour card** for €12 a month: one filter coffee every day. If you come in most mornings, it will cost you less than before.
- From April we will close on **Tuesdays** as well as Mondays, so our small team gets two days off together.

We know nobody likes paying more, especially now. We thought about using cheaper butter and smaller buns instead, and decided we would rather be honest with you about the price than quietly make things worse.

If you have questions, ask any of us at the counter, or come to the open evening on Thursday 26 February at 7 pm. There will be free buns, and we will listen.

With flour on our hands,
Tomás and Hanna, Linden & Rye
